desc: Derive the blocking condition precisely: building j (X_j < X_i) blocks i at height h iff the segment from (0,h) to (X_i, H_i) passes through/below (X_j, H_j), giving threshold h_{ij} = (H_j·X_i − H_i·X_j)/(X_i − X_j); i is invisible iff h ≤ max_{j<i} h_{ij}. Verify edge cases (h=0 visibility, ties).

Prove that the maximizing j for each i lies on the upper convex hull of points (X_j, H_j) (j<i), and that as we sweep i left to right, the relevant hull can be maintained incrementally with a monotone stack (slopes between consecutive hull points decreasing).

Implement the sweep: maintain hull of previous buildings; for each i, binary search the hull for the vertex j maximizing h_{ij} — equivalently find the hull edge whose slope comparison brackets the direction to (X_i, H_i); compute candidate h and take the global max. Use exact integer arithmetic (Fractions or cross-multiplication with __int128-equivalent via Python ints) to avoid precision issues, converting to float only at output.

Handle the output logic: let M = global maximum threshold. If all buildings visible at h=0 (equivalently M ≤ 0 and at h=0 nothing blocked — check sample 3 vs sample 2 distinction: M == 0 means answer 0.0; M < 0 means -1), print -1 if M < 0, else max(M, 0) with high precision formatting.

Test against the four samples plus adversarial cases: N=1 (answer -1 since single building always visible), collinear tops, strictly increasing heights, decreasing heights, large coordinates (1e9) for overflow/precision, and random brute-force cross-checks with an O(N²) verifier.
